source.title: When Does Generating More Help? Disentangling Fixed-Source Synthesis from Source Expansion in Synthetic Data Scaling
source.authors: Xu Guo; Jian Tong; Zhi-Hui Lu; Qi-Peng Guo

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a related scaling form in synthetic-data supervised fine-tuning: student test accuracy is measured as the response budget from a fixed source grows, and the form is forecast to a held-out budget. It does not test pretraining loss or parameter/token/compute scaling.
record.gate_note: The study measures mean@8 accuracy across response budgets, not held-out cross-entropy loss. Its matched-budget source comparisons and protocol audit are about synthetic-data allocation and protocol performance, not parameter/token/compute scaling. Results cited from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests a power-law residual in synthetic-data fine-tuning, P(r)=P∞−Ar^−α, and downstream accuracy predictability as response budget grows. These bear on V5 and V6. Appendix A.1 also gives specific mathematical conditions under which the curve is not a pure power law, bearing on V7. It does not test pretraining-loss scaling or orders-of-magnitude extrapolation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that fixed-source synthesis produces bounded, diminishing accuracy gains described by their fitted form; expanding real seed coverage becomes preferable at larger matched example budgets, and audited protocols give no consistent advantage over RS. Qualify the ceiling as model-derived and supported by finite-budget trends, rather than empirically established at infinite budget. Accuracy does not literally increase at every tested doubling.
record.recipe_differences: Adapts a rectified fine-tuning scaling form into an accuracy-versus-response-budget law for fixed-source synthetic-data SFT. It does not use the original pretraining loss measurement or parameter/token/compute sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes depend on teacher strength and source: the authors say the weaker teacher begins to flatten earlier, while the stronger teacher continues to rise. Some weakest-teacher cells slightly decline at the largest r.
record.code_released: not stated (the paper says code and data will be released, but gives no URL)
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), as stated in the supplied metadata
record.problems: Different outcome and scaling axis from the claim: mean@8 accuracy versus response budget rather than held-out cross-entropy versus parameters, tokens, or compute. The main response-budget range is r∈{1,2,4,8,16,32}; the held-out forecast is only from r≤16 to r=32. The study states that the power-law form is asymptotic and depends on a heavy-tail assumption; the empirical fits test the aggregate form, not the assumptions pointwise. Repeated SFT cells use 3 train seeds.
record.rows_left_out: RQ2 matched-budget seed-expansion/question-synthesis comparisons (Secs. 6 and 8; Figs. 4, 5, 7) and RQ3 protocol audits (Sec. 7; Fig. 6; Tables 5–6) are not separate rows because they compare source allocations or synthesis protocols rather than measuring the versions’ parameter/token/compute loss scaling or fixed-source response-budget curve. Table 3’s pooled forecast comparison against Carry and LogLin is not included as a separate row; the per-pair forecast errors are recorded in T3-* rows.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, training tokens or compute, including non-bottleneck conditions and several orders of magnitude.
Loss extrapolation from small runs to runs orders of magnitude larger; predicting r=32 from r≤16 does not test this.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its exponents; matched SFT-example budgets are not fixed-compute parameter/token optimisations.
Architecture changes at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities and training regimes beyond the tested synthetic-data reasoning SFT; cross-entropy loss scaling, broad scale ranges and direct verification of the latent-feature assumptions.
Downstream prediction from pretraining loss, parameter count or pretraining compute; generalisation beyond the tested reasoning benchmarks and response budgets.
Empirical sensitivity of fitted exponents to fitting methods, parameter counting, schedules or datasets; compute-optimal splits and explanations of disagreements between published pretraining laws.

missing.what: Mathematics full-grid fit errors for the four pair-specific power-law curves: 0.31, 0.29, 0.18 and 0.28 pp. These directly test functional-form agreement and are distinct from Table 3 forecasts.

Conditional mathematical results: a regularly varying feature tail yields a power law with a slowly varying multiplier; exposure probabilities bounded away from zero yield exponential saturation; separated exposure bands yield sums of exponentials. These are arguments, not measured failures in the experimental sweeps.
missing.locator: Appendix A.1, slowly varying correction and heavy-tail failure discussions.

record.verdict_notes: Use only the supplied text. Observed states for noninitial Table 2 points describe their contribution to the joint sweep, not independent proof of a power law or significant adjacent-budget gains. V5 concerns an offset power law in test error/accuracy residual, not cross-entropy loss. Fits have three parameters and only five training-budget points for forecasting; fitted exponents and ceilings are not reported. RQ2, RQ3, heterogeneous-source results and pooled extrapolator comparisons are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. The supplied text does not establish the record's EMNLP peer-review claim.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or sweep over model parameters, training tokens, or compute.
The study forecasts accuracy at r=32 from r≤16, but does not test loss prediction for runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute optimum over parameter count and token count is measured.
No architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.

Tests synthetic-data SFT in reasoning/STEM tasks using accuracy versus response budget. Does not test other modalities, repeated-data pretraining, fine-tuning transfer from pretraining, or loss scaling.
Measures downstream Mathematics and Physics benchmark accuracy versus fixed-source synthetic response budget, not downstream performance versus pretraining loss or model size.

Does not systematically vary parameter counting, training schedule, data, or fitting method to test exponent or compute-optimal-split dependence. It discusses assumptions and possible departures theoretically.

relationships.condition: Synthetic-data SFT on Mathematics and Physics, four teacher–student pairs, fixed source and training protocol, r=1–32.
relationships.reason: The offset power-law form fits Mathematics with MAE 0.18–0.31 pp and forecasts r=32 with errors 0.01–0.76 pp in T3-M-D31-Q7 through T3-P-Q72-L8; this supports a power-law residual to a fitted ceiling in this regime.
relationships.display_finding: The offset power law fit Mathematics with MAE 0.18–0.31 percentage points and forecast r = 32 with errors of 0.01–0.76 percentage points.

relationships.condition: DeepSeek-V3.1 teacher, both students and both domains, fixed-source response-budget scaling.
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises from r=1 to r=32 in all four sweeps, and T3-M-D31-Q7, T3-M-D31-L8, T3-P-D31-Q7 and T3-P-D31-L8 forecast the endpoint within 0.49–0.76 pp.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy rises as the response budget increases from 1 to 32 in all four sweeps, with endpoint forecast errors of 0.49–0.76 percentage points.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-72B teacher with Qwen2-7B student, both domains.
relationships.reason: Overall accuracy improves modestly, from 0.307 to 0.338 in Mathematics and 0.215 to 0.262 in Physics; T3-M-Q72-Q7 and T3-P-Q72-Q7 forecast r=32 within 0.30 and 0.01 pp.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy rises from 0.307 to 0.338 in mathematics and 0.215 to 0.262 in physics, with endpoint forecast errors of 0.30 and 0.01 percentage points.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-72B teacher with Llama-3.1-8B student, initial response-budget increases.
relationships.reason: Accuracy improves from r=1 to r=16 in both domains, with the bounded curve predicting the final endpoint within 0.67 and 0.29 pp in T3-M-Q72-L8 and T3-P-Q72-L8.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy improves as the response budget increases from 1 to 16 in both domains, with final endpoint prediction errors of 0.67 and 0.29 percentage points.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-72B teacher with Llama-3.1-8B student, r=16 to r=32.
relationships.reason: Further budget does not improve measured accuracy: T2-M-Q72-L8-r16/r32 change 0.341→0.340 and T2-P-Q72-L8-r16/r32 change 0.269→0.267, within reported variability.
relationships.display_finding: Increasing synthesis budget from r=16 to r=32 changed accuracy from 0.341 to 0.340 and from 0.269 to 0.267, within reported variability.

relationships.condition: Conditional mathematical argument within the fixed-source feature-coverage model.
relationships.reason: Appendix A.1, not captured by existing rows, derives slowly varying corrections, exponential saturation or sums of exponentials when the pure power-tail assumption changes; monotone diminishing returns alone therefore do not imply a single power law.
relationships.display_finding: Changing the pure power-tail assumption yielded slowly varying corrections, exponential saturation or sums of exponentials, so monotone diminishing returns did not imply a single power law.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Fixed-source synthetic-data SFT response-budget sweeps in Mathematics and Physics, four teacher–student pairs
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy increases with r and the authors report diminishing returns; the fixed-source curve predicts the held-out r=32 point in the tested cells (rows T2-* and T3-*). This supports only this fine-tuning setting and metric, not pretraining-loss laws.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Test accuracy on the study’s Mathematics and Physics tasks as fixed-source response budget grows
reader_labels.reason: The reported response-budget curves rise across the tested settings and the authors describe the trend as predictable with diminishing gains; the test is limited to this accuracy metric and these tasks (rows T2-* and T3-*).
